title: Products and dimension growth of smooth connected solvable normal subgroups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. A group scheme is solvable if it has a finite descending series of closed subgroup schemes, each normal in its predecessor, with commutative group-scheme quotients. Let $G$ be smooth and geometrically connected and let $H,N\subseteq G$ be smooth connected normal solvable subgroup schemes. Their product is represented by a smooth connected normal solvable subgroup $HN\subseteq G$, containing both $H$ and $N$, with the pointwise description that $x\in(HN)(A)$ if and only if $x\in H(B)N(B)$ after some faithfully flat finitely presented $A$-algebra $B$. A smooth connected group scheme over a field remains smooth and connected after every field extension, and a solvable group scheme remains solvable after every field extension. For a closed inclusion $J\subsetneq L$ of smooth connected group schemes one has $\dim J<\dim L$; these dimensions are nonnegative integers, bounded above by $\dim G$ for subgroup schemes of $G$. Here dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

source.place: Section 5(f), product construction and Theorem 5.52, printed pp.111--112; Proposition 6.27, printed p.131; Lemma 6.41 and the greatest-dimension argument in Proposition 6.42, printed p.134; Propositions 1.34--1.36 and 1.62, on connected group varieties and field extension.

proof.text: Form $q:G\to Q=G/N$ by [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Factor $q|_H$ as a faithfully flat finitely presented homomorphism $r:H\to I$ followed by a closed immersion $I\hookrightarrow Q$, using [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]. Its kernel is the scheme-theoretic intersection $K=H\times_GN$, so $I\simeq H/K$ as fppf sheaves. In particular $I$ is affine of finite type, since it is closed in the affine scheme $Q$. Put $P=q^{-1}(I)$. The quotient node gives a closed subgroup $P\subseteq G$ and an exact sequence $1\to N\to P\to I\to1$. The kernel $K$ need not be smooth; no such hypothesis was used.

source.place: Theorem 5.39, p.108; Section 5(f), Theorem 5.52 and Proposition 5.54, pp.111–112.

proof.text: For a commutative $k$-algebra $A$, a point $x\in P(A)$ has $q(x)\in I(A)$. The affine fibre product $H\times_{I,q(x)}\operatorname{Spec}A=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the base change of $r$, so $B$ is a faithfully flat finitely presented $A$-algebra. Its tautological point is $h\in H(B)$ with $q(h)=q(x_B)$. Hence $h^{-1}x_B\in N(B)$ by the kernel assertion for $q$, giving $x_B\in H(B)N(B)$. Conversely, if $x_B=h n$, then $q(x)_B=q(h)\in I(B)$, and the defining closed-subscheme equations of $I$ vanish already over $A$, since $A\to B$ is injective. Hence $x\in P(A)$. This also shows $H,N\subseteq P$. For $g\in G(A)$, conjugating the displayed factorization gives $g_Bx_Bg_B^{-1}=(g_Bhg_B^{-1})(g_Bng_B^{-1})\in H(B)N(B)$ by normality of both subgroups. The converse just proved gives $gxg^{-1}\in P(A)$; applying it to $g^{-1}$ proves equality. Thus $P$ is normal in $G$, and we define $HN=P$.

source.place: Section 5(f), product functor preceding Theorem 5.52, p.111; Proposition 5.54, p.112.

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected], the identity section makes connected $H$ geometrically connected. Apply the quotient assertions of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to $H/K\simeq I$: the quotient $I$ is smooth and geometrically connected. Apply the inverse-image assertion of that same node to $P=q^{-1}(I)$, with the smooth connected groups $N$ and $I$. It follows that $P$ is smooth and connected. This proves the geometric properties without assuming the intersection $K$ smooth.

source.place: Propositions 1.34–1.36, pp.16–17; Proposition 1.62, p.24; Proposition 5.59, p.114; Lemma 6.41, p.134.

proof.text: Choose a solvable series $H=H_0\triangleright H_1\triangleright\cdots\triangleright H_a=1$. For each $i$, factor $H_i\to I$ through its closed image $I_i$, using [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]. Thus $I_0=I$, $I_a=1$, and points of $I_i$ lift fppf locally to $H_i$. For $u\in I_i(A)$ and $v\in I_{i+1}(A)$, lift both over a common fppf cover. Normality of $H_{i+1}$ in $H_i$ puts $uvu^{-1}$ in $I_{i+1}$ after the cover, hence over $A$ by its closed equations. So $I_{i+1}\triangleleft I_i$. Form $I_i/I_{i+1}$ with [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry]. Any two sections of this quotient lift fppf locally first to $I_i$ and then to $H_i$. Their commutator then lies in $H_{i+1}$ because $H_i/H_{i+1}$ is commutative, and so its image in $I_i/I_{i+1}$ is the identity. Sheaf descent proves that the quotient is commutative. Consequently $(I_i)$ is a solvable series for $I$.

source.place: Proposition 6.27, p.131 (image of a solvable series); Theorem 5.55, p.113.

proof.text: Let $P_i$ be the inverse image of $I_i$ under $P\to I=P/N$. The correspondence assertion of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] gives $P_{i+1}\triangleleft P_i$ and $P_i/P_{i+1}\simeq I_i/I_{i+1}$. Thus $P=P_0\triangleright\cdots\triangleright P_a=N$ has commutative successive quotients. Append the given solvable series of $N$. This is a finite series ending in $1$, proving $HN=P$ solvable, including when either initial series has length zero.

source.place: Proposition 6.27, p.131 (inverse-image and concatenation argument); Lemma 6.41, p.134.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any smooth connected group scheme occurring in the statement and let $K/k$ be a field extension. Its identity is a rational section, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] gives connectedness of $L_K$. Clause (2) of [lem-pc-proper-base-change] gives smoothness of $L_K$. For any solvable affine finite-type group $S$, base change a chosen finite solvable series. Closed immersions remain closed immersions because on affine coordinate algebras they are surjections and tensor product preserves surjections; normality and commutativity are identities on the functors of points and remain so after restriction to $K$-algebras. By the field-extension assertion of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], each new successive quotient is the base change of the old commutative quotient. The series still ends in $1$, so $S_K$ is solvable.

source.place: Proposition 1.34 and Summary 1.36, pp.16–17; Corollary 6.31, p.132; smooth base change: Stacks 01VB, morphisms.tex lemma-base-change-smooth.

proof.text: For a closed inclusion $J\subsetneq L$ as in the statement, [lem-wf-smooth-components-disjoint] identifies the irreducible components of the smooth affine finite-type scheme $L$ with its connected components. Since $L$ is connected, it is irreducible. It is reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Write $L=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $J=\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak a)$. If their underlying spaces were equal, every element of $\mathfrak a$ would belong to every prime of $R$, hence would be nilpotent; reducedness of $R$ forces $\mathfrak a=0$, contrary to proper inclusion. Therefore $|J|\subsetneq|L|$ is a proper closed subset of the irreducible affine variety $L$. Apply [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop] to obtain $\dim J<\dim L$.

source.place: Corollary 1.35 and dimension discussion, pp.17–18; greatest-dimension argument of Proposition 6.42, p.134.

proof.text: Every group scheme in question is nonempty, since it has its identity point. Its dimension is therefore at least zero by the definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. It is finite by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], hence is a nonnegative integer. If $S\subseteq G$ is a closed subgroup, any strict chain of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $S$ is also such a chain in $G$, because $S$ is closed. Taking suprema proves $\dim S\le\dim G$. These observations give all dimension bounds in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-beaccf1a2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full. The item is unchanged, and the delivery has no new nodes and no fixes; proof_deps equals the union of the step uses (9 nodes). There is no re-split repair note and no SGA citation. I checked the route against Milne iAG2017 in the literature PDF: Thm 5.52, Prop 5.54, Prop 6.27, Lemma 6.41 and Prop 6.42. The steps write out 6.41 and 6.27 over an arbitrary field. Step 1: HN=q^{-1}(I), where I is the closed image of H in G/N given by the factorization node; affine implies separated, and the kernel is H x_G N. Step 2: B = H x_I Spec A is faithfully flat and finitely presented over A; the iff holds for every faithfully flat B, and normality follows by conjugating h and n separately. Step 3: 04KV plus the quotient node's smooth/geometrically connected clause and its inverse-image clause; K=H∩N is not assumed smooth. Step 4: the image series is checked with common faithfully flat lifts and the kernel clause. Step 5: correspondence clause plus N's series. Step 6: base change of connectedness (04KV), smoothness (proper-base-change clause 2) and solvable series (quotient node's field-extension clause). Step 7: smooth gives regular local rings, so L is irreducible, and L is reduced, so a proper J has a proper underlying closed set; then affine dimension drop. Step 8: dimension is finite and nonnegative, and chains in a closed S are chains in G. Edge cases checked: trivial H or N, H=N, series of length 0, G_a^2 with kernel α_p, and α_p ⊇ 1 for why reducedness is needed. These match what the citer lem-sfb-reductive-radical-quotient uses. No duplicate in the DAG. The six generic-geometry tool_uses are accepted. One advisory: step 7 does not write out the one-line identification of prime-chain dimension with topological Krull dimension.
